annotations.text:
Mirrors brink's two doors: opening IS choosing what you work in.

Unlike brink there is one identity, the project, so recents carry no kind badge and there is no door for a loose map file (decided 2026-09-14).
Texel density is asked at creation because it is the one setting every sheet is checked against afterwards. Changing it later is a project-wide event, not a field.

The project name in the top bar is the door into the project: maps, new map, settings. No binder dock — papercut's frame has a rail and an inspector, and the map list is short.

The Materials section in the inspector stays for picking; editing moves to Project settings.
LDtk's Tilesets tab, in our terms: the project LISTS its images, so a missing or mis-sized one is a row with a status, not a blank texture (#148).

Terrain type management. Tags stay in the sidecar beside the PNG; this section reads them. The tile tagger itself is #146 and not drawn here.

The Transitions list is the project-wide 'to author' count.
DECIDED 2026-09-14: materials are a project setting. The library lives in papercut.json; a map stores only the ids its voxels hold. The app opens projects only, so a map never needs a fallback.

DECIDED 2026-09-14: one resolution profile per project, no per-map override; sheets are checked against it, never rescaled.

DECIDED 2026-09-14: papercut.json lists maps in order; a file in maps/ but not the list is reported.
